title: feat: open upstream model probe and endpoint test to every account
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
Split out of #13464 so the policy change gets reviewed on its own.

- Drops the publish-allowlist gate from `POST /community-endpoints/models` and `/test`. The pre-existing 30s per-account-per-kind throttle is now the only limiter.
- Un-hides "Fetch models" and "Test endpoint" in the My Models dialog, so a non-allowlisted owner can probe an upstream before saving a private model instead of typing the model ID blind.
- Updates the OpenAPI descriptions, the allowlist 403 message, and the docs sentences that said probing needs approval.
- Rewrites the denied-account test to stub the upstream and assert the returned model IDs, replacing a bare `403` expectation.

Scope note: it reverses part of #12333, which deliberately kept the allowlist on the probes. It widens who can make the enter Worker issue an outbound HTTPS request to a caller-supplied host with a caller-supplied bearer token — bounded by the existing https-only + private-host blocklist in `normalizeCommunityEndpointBaseUrl`, `redirect: "manual"` in the probe client, and the throttle.

gist.headline: Every hive gets a probe
gist.blurb: The model workbench is open to every account now. Fetch the upstream catalog, test the connection, then plant a private model with fewer guesses involved.
gist.summary: Opened the community endpoint model-fetch and endpoint-test tools to every account, retaining the existing 30-second per-account, per-kind throttle while removing the publishing allowlist requirement.
gist.impact: Owners can now fetch upstream model IDs and test a private community endpoint directly from My Models before saving it, rather than entering model IDs blind.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Polli as a careful garden technician opening a small greenhouse gate to a community-endpoint testing bench. A retro terminal fetches a neat catalog of model-name seed packets while friendly code-plants grow from pots; the scene represents every account being able to inspect and verify an upstream before planting a private model.
